verses.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
All a man's ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even the man's enemies live at peace with him.
Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
A man's heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.
Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
Wicked behavior is detestable to kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
Righteous lips are a king's delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.
The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
When a king's face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.
The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.
Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
A worker's appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.
A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

context.author: Solomon, named in the heading “The proverbs of Solomon” (10:1). The collection runs from 10:1 to 22:16, about 375 sayings.
context.genre: Wisdom sayings: two-line proverbs, most of them contrasts
context.audience: Anyone learning to live wisely, first the young men of Israel’s court and households
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: This chapter gathers sayings about God’s rule over human plans. “The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD” (v.1). Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be established (v.3). “A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps” (v.9). A run of sayings about the king follows (vv.10-15), and then the best known of all: “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall” (v.18). Gracious words are like honey (v.24), gray hair is a crown of glory (v.31), and “the lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD” (v.33).
context.custom: Lots were small stones or sticks cast or drawn to make decisions, and Israel used them to divide the land (Joshua 18:10) and to choose for office (1 Samuel 10:20-21). The priest carried the Urim and Thummim in his breastpiece for seeking God’s answer (Exodus 28:30). Kings were expected to judge justly (vv.10-13), and the balances and weights were under the king’s and God’s care (v.11).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 17 begins: better a dry crust with peace than a house full of feasting with strife.
context.timelineBible: The apostles cast lots to choose Matthias in Acts 1:26, the last time lots are used in the Bible. Haman’s pride before his fall in Esther 5-7 and Nebuchadnezzar’s in Daniel 4 are stories of v.18. James 4:13-15 warns, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that” (James 4:15).

translation.meaning: Arrangements, things set in order. A person sets his plans in order, but God gives the answer.
To roll. “Roll your works onto the LORD,” as one rolls a heavy load.
A stone or token cast to make a decision. The LORD decides how it falls.

gospelParallels.note: If the Lord is willing, we will do this or that.
The apostles cast lots for Matthias.
Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled.

otBackground.note: Joshua divides the land by lot.
Haman hangs on the gallows he built.

overview.summary: People make plans, but the LORD directs their steps; pride goes before a fall, and every decision of the lot is from the LORD.
overview.settingLine: Sayings about God, the king and human plans.

history.t: The king judged and kept fair weights.
Lots and the Urim and Thummim.

customs.t: Stones thrown into a fold of cloth.

archaeology.t: Seal impressions reading lmlk (meaning belonging to the king) are stamped on jar handles from Judah.
Beehives found at Tel Rehov show that Israel kept bees about 900 BC.

overview.discussion: “A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps” (v.9). Where do I need to plan well and then hold my plans loosely?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (10:1)
